title: I Love the Drop of Water Balanced on the Flat Leaf...
text:
I love the drop of water balanced on the flat leaf,

trembling in the wind. In the ocean of air the whole

universe vibrates in secret, and she in her isolation.

Her simple crystal contains the form,

in the uncertain instant: ready to fall,

ready to remain—limpid, exact.

And the leaf is a small desert for the immensity of the act.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Meireles's poised drop as a tiny isolated act containing a whole vibrating universe.

title: Portrait
text:
I did not have this face of today,

so calm, so sad, so thin,

nor these eyes so empty,

nor this bitter lip.


I did not have these strengthless hands,

so still and cold and dead;

I did not have this heart

that does not even show itself.


I did not notice this change,

so simple, so certain, so easy:

In what mirror was

my image lost?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the famous self-portrait's quiet shock before aging and estrangement from one's own image.

title: Here My Life Is...
text:
Here my life is;

this sand so clear, with designs

of wanderings dedicated to the wind.


Here my voice is;

this empty shell,

shadow of sound

that suffers its own lament.

Here is my pain. This broken coral,

surviving its poetic moment.

Here is my inheritance

—this solitary sea that on one side was love,

and on the other was forgetting.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the shore objects as life, voice, pain, inheritance, love, and oblivion.

title: Before Your Gaze...
text:
Before your gaze,

there was not, nor will there be after-spring.

Because we live from what endures

and not from what we were.

From that perhaps of the loved and seen:

the Creator's term in the creature...

I am not I, but rather the perfume that preserves me in you,

and sums up the remainder the hours corrode.

But do not weep: in my day there is more dream and wisdom

than in the vague centuries of man.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the source's strange after-spring compound and the speaker as perfume preserved in another.

title: What Sang Yesterday...
text:
What sang yesterday

No longer sings.

It died with a flower in its mouth:

In that of the thorn in its throat.


It loved water without thirst

And, certainly,

Despite having wings, it watched time

Free of need.


It was not longing or imprudence:

It was nothing.

And the day touches in silence

The misfortune caused.


If perhaps that is misfortune:

To lose one's life

Over so beautiful a rose,

For so slight a wound.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the fragile death-by-rose image and the source's uncertain judgment of misfortune.
